findings.evidence: template/scripts/execute_requirement.py:539-540 short-circuits _contribution_publication_supported when legacy_receipts is true. advance has no earlier lifecycle_mode call, and the subsequent loop can consume receipts or start managed children (lines 579-598). This contradicts the active completion-lifecycle requirement that unsupported source combinations fail at selection and never switch to the legacy path.
findings.summary: Resuming a multi-child Requirement with legacy receipts bypasses contract selection, allowing unsupported source configurations to continue through the legacy path.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/project_publish.py:519 selects portable mode, but validate_shared_manifest at lines 453-455 imports requirement_contributions for a version-two manifest without checking that mode; requirement_contributions.py:15 imports lifecycle_workers at module level. The subsequent publication branch at project_publish.py:550-552 also imports requirement_composition, whose line 15 imports lifecycle_workers. Thus a downstream publication request loads coordinator modules or fails with ImportError instead of rejecting the coordinator-only request before import, contrary to the active lifecycle-workers requirement.
findings.summary: Portable publication can still load the coordinator stack when given a version-two shared manifest.
